preconditions.description: Input is a single integer n where 1 ≤ n ≤ 10³.

postconditions.description: Output consists of exactly n lines, each containing two integers representing coordinates.

postconditions.expression: len({tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdout.strip().splitlines()}) == n
postconditions.description: All n knight coordinates are unique (no duplicates).

postconditions.expression: all(-10**9 <= int(x) <= 10**9 and -10**9 <= int(y) <= 10**9 for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for x, y in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: Each coordinate (xᵢ, yᵢ) satisfies -10⁹ ≤ xᵢ, yᵢ ≤ 10⁹.
The initial placement guarantees that the final number of knights is at least ⌊n²/10⌋ (always true for n ≥ 1).

postconditions.expression: all(knight != (x, y) for knight in initial_knights for x, y in final_knights if knight != (x, y))
postconditions.description: The final placement (after all additions) includes all initial knights and any newly added knights, where initial_knights is the set of output coordinates and final_knights is the set of all knights after the process terminates (implied by construction).

The final number of knights (after all additions) is at least ⌊n²/10⌋, where final_knights is the set of all knights after the process terminates (implied by the problem's guarantee and construction).
